Hollow Knight is a beautifully crafted Metroidvania that blends tight combat, rich exploration, and haunting atmosphere into an unforgettable experience. Set in the fallen underground kingdom of Hallownest, the game drops you into a vast, interconnected world with minimal guidance, trusting you to carve your own path forward.

Exploration is the heart of the game. Every new movement ability—whether it’s a dash, double jump, or wall climb—unlocks previously unreachable areas, making backtracking feel rewarding rather than repetitive. The map design is intricate and cleverly layered, filled with secrets, optional bosses, and hidden story threads that reward curiosity.

Combat starts simple but grows increasingly demanding. Boss fights are a standout feature: fast-paced, pattern-driven, and often brutally challenging. Victory rarely comes easily, but each win feels earned through skill and persistence rather than luck.

Artistically, Hollow Knight shines. Its hand-drawn environments are moody and atmospheric, blending melancholy with quiet beauty. The soundtrack complements this perfectly, enhancing both the loneliness of exploration and the intensity of combat.

While the difficulty can be steep—especially in late-game content—the challenge is part of its identity. For players who enjoy precision platforming, deep exploration, and rewarding combat, Hollow Knight stands as one of the strongest entries in the modern Metroidvania genre.

It's a bautiful soulslike metroidvania. Graphics are well-made, the lore is deep and interesting and the gameplay is stellar. It's suitable for new players of this genre and veterans alike due to providing an easy start and very hard optional challenges.
For those who look for the story, this game is very non-linear. There are many ways you can go at any time, so you can explore the world in the way you want. This includes being able to skip large portions if you don't want to explore them, although I highly recommend exploring all parts of the game anyways simply because there are always interesting things to find.
The game also has an active modding community so you can expand your gameplay experience even more, be it with multiplayer, borderline unfair bosses to fight or insane platforming.
The only thing you should know before jumping in is that after the starting area the game can become much more difficult more quickly and there are no in-game tutorials on the basic mechanics that you have from the beginning so if you are new to this genre you may want to look up a guide on them

Let's talk about Hollow Knight.

From my point of view, Hollow Knight is an experience, the experience of exploring a vast kingdom you don't know anything about, why are you here you ask? You don't know either, you just arrived here with a weapon and the ability to heal yourself.

Along the game you encounter various NPCs, zones, bosses and enemies that tell you in a way what happened to Hallownest, and that's the greatest thing about it, you're free to do what you want. You can just explore and see the beauty of the kingdom until you find an actual objective, and that's part of Hollow Knight's Charm (hehe)

From it's lovable characters, to story, visuals and beautiful soundtrack, Hollow Knight is a masterpiece.

I said enough, now give it a try, the game has some difficulty to it, but if you like those kind of games, you won't regret it :)

Not sure what else I can say about this game which hasn't already been said by so many others, but I will say this is single-handedly the best Metroidvania I've ever played. I adored the sound design, visuals, gameplay, and it has some of the greatest bosses I've ever fought in a game.

This is also one of the hardest games I've ever played, but to me, it never felt cheap. It's the perfect balance of difficulty, and I can't express enough just how satisfying it was defeating some of the harder bosses and getting past the more challenging platforming sections.

The lore of this game is also super deep and I would highly recommend checking out Mossbag on YouTube if you want to learn more about it. (Just be weary of spoilers, of course!)

As for negatives, the backtracking could get quite annoying at times, but it was never unbearable for me. Many people have criticised the map system, but I personally never had a major problem with it. I can 100% understand why it would be a deal breaker for some though.

Hollow Knight gets a 9/10 from me. Would highly, HIGHLY recommend to anyone even remotely interested. And it's cheap, too; Only $15.00 when not on sale, and trust me, that is the very definition of a steal.

Thank you, Team Cherry, for this masterpiece. Now please give us Silksong, I need it badly...

Absolutely phenomenal game with beautiful visuals and music. It can be a challenging at times, but the platforming and combat system work so well together that playing it is a truly joyful experience. Dying didn't have the same frustration as other games; every hit gives you a split second to take in what you did wrong and correct your approach next time. Backtracking can be mitigated with a plethora of tools, and the levels are always designed with quiet atmospheric moments, sometimes with NPC conversations sprinkled along your path. The sound effects are punchy when they need to be, and fit the environment they're found in seamlessly.

I don't usually latch onto a game because of it's difficulty, but Hollow Knight delivers just enough to feel rewarding without being unapproachable. Understanding how your actions affect your momentum is the key to manoeuvring around environmental and enemy hazards. Speaking of enemies, the bosses are really fun to fight, having clearly telegraphed attacks with audio/visual cues and discernible patterns.

If you want a memorable Metroidvania with a unique challenge and stellar presentation that's more than worth the price of admission, this is it!

One of the few games I consider a true masterpiece. The experience of delving into the captivating world of Hallownest is truly amazing. It offers an abundance of wonders waiting to be discovered. Many different areas/biomes, over 150 unique enemies, over 40 formidable bosses, and countless secrets. And, of course, it follows the beloved Metroidvania formula, providing a steady stream of new abilities and upgrades.

The game's unique theme centered around insects and especially bugs is an aspect I truly adore. It gives Hollow Knight an almost unrivaled charm. This is also enhanced by its amazing hand drawn art style.

The game is challenging with some brutal bosses. However, by selectively engaging with only the required bosses and taking a slow and steady approach, I believe that the standard completion of the game is not excessively difficult and can be enjoyable for a wide audience. And for those seeking big challenges, Hollow Knight has tons of those. It's important to acknowledge that there are occasional moments of frustration, such as the unnecessarily long boss run backs. But in the end the difficulty is much more rewarding than it is frustrating

After finishing Guacamelee 2, I had an itch for metroidvanias. At the recommendation of my friends, I bought this, which was around 10 dollars at the time. With these almost 10 dollars, I have accumulated over 60 hours of gameplay, and I'm still not completely finished yet. Everything about this game is simply outstanding, from the music, visuals, gameplay, and story/characters. Not once in my time playing did I ever feel bored or displeased with this game. Exploration is rewarding, and abilities gained feel natural. The challenging bosses and enemies provide the utmost satisfaction when finally conquered, and that goes double for the incredibly nerve-wracking (and sharp) platforming segments in White Palace. My only regret is not buying this game when it came out to see it grow into its current state, but even then it still feels great to experience the complete package.
